name: Snow and Stories
tagline: Four full Tokyo days of anime and one big car day, a fast Kansai part from one base, then 7 nights in Hokkaido with ski-in Niseko, the drift course and Sapporo.
summary: Tokyo 4 nights: Akihabara, Ikebukuro, Nakano and a SHELTER live show, the Girls Band Cry walk in Kawasaki, and one rental-car day for Fuji, the Hakone passes and Daikoku. Then the Nozomi to Osaka for 3 nights from one Namba hotel: the Nara hill fire (Sat 23), Kyoto's Sabbat places, and the Suzuka EV kart (Mon 25). On Jan 26 you fly to New Chitose and sleep 4 nights at a ski-in hotel at Niseko Annupuri, where Pegasis teaches Aoki on the beginner runs and drives the Rusutsu snow course. The last 3 nights are in Sapporo, with Asahiyama's penguins. Only 4 hotels in 14 nights.

who.pegasis: IN (all 25 wants but 2): Daikoku with you driving (Thu night, no guide), Hakone Turnpike, Taikanzan, Otome Pass, Gotemba outlets, free City Hall view, Narita bus instead of N'EX, Isetan half-price food (night 1), Golden Gai/Omoide Yokocho, SHELTER with a live show, Nakano, Radio Kaikan, Ikebukuro goods, Maidreamin (Shibuya and Sapporo), Nara hill fire, Suzuka EV kart, Rusutsu drift (you drive the 15:00 course, after the licence email), Niseko, Asahiyama penguins, Daruma, Moiwa, GARAKU. OUT: Onuma (on the Hakodate side, not on this route) and the Tokaido car road west (this plan takes the Shinkansen; only Suzuka is kept). New for your one backpack: warm layers on night 1 in Shinjuku, goggles and gloves at Gotemba, full ski rental with ski wear at Rhythm, a suitcase from Don Quijote that goes ahead to Sapporo with goods and souvenirs only (all ski and warm gear stays in the backpack with you), and 4 laundry nights, all in the hotels.
who.aoki: IN: Omoide Yokocho, Daikoku (and Tatsumi PA if open), Lake Kawaguchi, the Eva road through Sengokuhara to Lake Ashi, Yokohama Chinatown (Cup Noodles Museum is out: it closes 18:00), Suga stairs, Shimokitazawa, SHELTER live show, Nakano, Akihabara ZEST and Radio Kaikan, Ikebukuro goods, used goods, free City Hall view, Girls Band Cry Tokyo Station dome, Hachiko and the Kawasaki walk (Miharashi, Lazona, East Exit plaza, Marufuku, CLUB CITTA') with the stamp book (bought in Kawasaki; the online shop does not ship abroad), Shibuya Sky before 15:00, Nintendo/Pokémon Shibuya, maid café, Don Quijote coupon, Nara fire, Fushimi Inari at dawn, Kinkakuji, Sabbat of the Witch in Kyoto, Namba food, Den Den Town, Liberty Walk, Suzuka, Niseko first ski days (Pegasis teaches you on the Family course and the Dream No.1 Quad; no ski school, no lessons), Rusutsu drift ride (rear seat in Pegasis's course), Daruma, Moiwa. OUT: Enoshima/Slam Dunk, Yuru Camp Motosu and the Hanz villa (only one car day, no Fuji night), Fujiten ski (Hokkaido snow is better), Fuji Motorsports Museum and Nissan Crossing (Pegasis not interested), Toyota day in Nagoya, the Kobe and Grand Front Sabbat places (the Kansai part is fast), Cape Kamui (winter path closed), Aokana/Goto (far). No onsen bathing is planned for either of you; the hotels have a bath in the room.

Turnpike ¥900, fuel, parking ≈ ¥18,000, Nozomi ≈ ¥14,900, Kansai trains incl. Suzuka (Kintetsu ¥3,510 each way) and Liberty Walk ≈ ¥16,000, Rapi:t ¥1,670, Jetstar ¥7,510, Hokkaido 4WD 4 days + fuel ≈ ¥27,000 each, JR Asahikawa ¥10,880, airport train ¥1,230). Aoki adds about ¥3,000–5,000 for a checked bag on Spring Airlines and ≈ ¥2,500 on Jetstar; Pegasis adds ¥2,520 for the Shikotsu bus.

cost.activities: Pegasis ≈ ¥125,000 (ski rental 3 days with wear ≈ ¥39,000 with the online discount, lifts ≈ ¥33,000 (Annupuri day, Rusutsu 5 h online ¥11,600, all-mountain day), Rusutsu 30-min Introduction drive ¥31,000, Suzuka, Shibuya Sky, SHELTER, maid cafés, temples, Moiwa, zoo, Shikotsu) · Aoki ≈ ¥90,000 (same rental, lifts ≈ ¥22,000–26,000, drift rear seat ¥10,000, the rest similar; no ski lessons)

flights: Pegasis: open-jaw about CA$1,247 (drafts, Sep 2026). Out: WestJet Toronto 09:35 Mon Jan 18 → Calgary → Narita 16:30 Tue Jan 19 (backpack only: no checked bag needed). Home: Air Canada New Chitose 19:35 Tue Feb 2 → Vancouver → Toronto 19:57 same day (Google Flights, Sep 26, 2026: ¥80,050 one way). Checked bag home: Air Canada's allowance depends on the fare type; check it in the baggage calculator when you book, and choose a fare with 1 checked bag for the suitcase (not checked here; if a fee applies, budget about CA$100).

Aoki: in: Spring Airlines Shanghai Pudong 15:00 → Narita 18:40 Tue Jan 19 (Google Flights, Sep 26, 2026: ¥32,840 base fare with a small cabin bag only: choose a fare with a checked bag, about ¥3,000–5,000 more). Home: Spring Airlines New Chitose 13:50 → Shanghai Pudong 17:00 Tue Feb 2, nonstop (¥83,340, Chinese New Year prices). There is no Spring nonstop on Mon Feb 1; the cheapest Feb 1 option was Jetstar via Narita ¥51,250, arriving 01:10 the next day. Book early.
Osaka → Hokkaido: Jetstar Kansai 09:50 → New Chitose 11:50, Tue Jan 26 (Google Flights, Sep 26, 2026: ¥7,510; + checked bag about ¥2,500 for Aoki). Backup: Peach Kansai 09:15 → 11:10 (¥10,150).

bookFirst.what: Toyota Rent a Car, both cars: (1) Shinjuku-sanchome, Thu Jan 21 08:00 → Fri Jan 22 08:00, compact with studless tyres (¥2,200/24 h) + ETC card (¥550); (2) New Chitose Airport Poplar → Sapporo-ekimae, Jan 26 13:00 → Jan 30 about 14:30, 4WD
bookFirst.why: book NOW (late Sep 2026): Toyota takes bookings 6 months ahead and cancelling is free up to 7 days before pick-up. Tokyo shops have few studless cars: after booking, phone the Shinjuku-sanchome shop (03-3341-2603) to confirm a studless car. 4WD cars at CTS sell out in the ski season.

bookFirst.what: Niseko Northern Resort An'nupuri, Jan 26–30, deluxe twin (or ask for the standard twin with separate beds), dinner + breakfast, on the official site (90-day early-bird plan, ¥282,600 for 2)
bookFirst.why: book NOW, by Oct 28 at the latest (90-day early-bird ends): the official site showed '1 room left' on Sep 26 and Niseko is almost full for late January. Jalan was ¥303,808 for the same room.

bookFirst.what: Rusutsu snow drift: email activity@rusutsu.co.jp (tel 0136-46-3332) now to ask if Pegasis's 1-year licence + IDP is accepted; then book the Thu Jan 28 15:00 Introduction course (¥31,000, Aoki in the rear seat ¥10,000)
bookFirst.why: email NOW (the answer decides if Pegasis drives or you both take the ¥17,000-per-person pro ride); book after the answer and by early January. A 10% cancellation fee applies from the moment of booking (50% from the day before).

bookFirst.what: All flights: Pegasis's open-jaw (with 1 checked bag home), Aoki's Spring Airlines both ways with a checked bag, Jetstar KIX → CTS on Jan 26
bookFirst.why: book by Oct 15, because Chinese New Year pushes Aoki's Feb 2 fare up and the ¥7,510 Jetstar fare will not last.

bookFirst.what: Hotels: Super Hotel Shinjuku Kabukicho (Jan 19–23), Dormy Inn PREMIUM Namba ANNEX (Jan 23–26, free-cancellation rate), Route-Inn Sapporo Ekimae Kitaguchi (Jan 30–Feb 2)
bookFirst.why: book by Oct 15, because the Nara fire Saturday fills Osaka and the Sapporo twin plans showed '1 room left'. In November, check the official Nara page for the Jan 23 hill-fire date before the free cancellation ends.

bookFirst.what: Rhythm ski rental for both (3 days Jan 27–29, skis + boots + poles + helmet + jacket + pants), pick-up at Rhythm Hirafu on Wed Jan 27 morning
bookFirst.why: book online by Oct 31, 2026: the 10% online discount (code shown on the Rhythm site) ends that day.

bookFirst.what: Suzuka EV kart (Mon Jan 25, Asoview) and SHELTER show ticket (Wed Jan 20)
bookFirst.why: on Dec 1, 2026 the January kart times come out (plan for about 12:30, the karts run only about 12:00–13:15); book at once. The SHELTER January list also comes out in December: if Jan 20 has no show, swap day 2 and day 4.

bookFirst.what: Shibuya Sky web ticket, Fri Jan 22, 14:40 slot
bookFirst.why: book on Jan 8, 2027 (tickets open 2 weeks ahead): the before-15:00 slots are cheaper (¥2,700) and sell out.

bookFirst.what: Email Route-Inn Sapporo Ekimae Kitaguchi to accept Pegasis's suitcase parcel (Yamato, delivery date Jan 29, for a Jan 30 check-in)
bookFirst.why: ask by Jan 15, 2027, because the hotel must agree to keep a guest parcel before check-in.

places.blurb: Both of you land here on Tue Jan 19. Pegasis lands first (WestJet 16:30) and goes ahead to Shinjuku to buy winter clothes; Aoki lands at 18:40 (Spring Airlines).

info.label: To Tokyo
info.value: Airport Bus TYO-NRT to Tokyo Station, ¥1,500, about 70–80 min

tips: Check which terminal each flight uses. A free shuttle bus runs between the terminals.
Pegasis: while you wait, buy two Welcome Suica cards and eat something. Register both of you in Visit Japan Web before the flights.
The ¥1,500 bus needs no booking. Late-night buses cost ¥3,000, so take one before about 22:00.

places.ja: 東京駅 丸の内南口ドーム
places.blurb: The round brick hall where Nina arrives in Tokyo in Girls Band Cry episode 1. The airport bus stops at Tokyo Station, so it costs only 10 minutes.

info.label: From the bus stop
info.value: Walk through the station to the Marunouchi side, 5–8 min

tips: Look up at the dome ceiling: eagles and the Chinese zodiac animals.

places.ja: スーパーホテル新宿歌舞伎町
places.blurb: A good-value business hotel in Kabukicho, 7 minutes from Shinjuku Station, with a free breakfast buffet. You sleep here 4 nights, Jan 19–22.

info.label: Room
info.value: Economy twin (two 90 cm beds) with breakfast

info.label: Price
info.value: ¥69,800 for 4 nights, 2 people (Jalan, vacancy seen Sep 26, 2026) = about ¥34,900 per person

info.label: Laundry
info.value: Coin laundry in the hotel (washer ¥100, dryer free)

tips: Book on Jalan or the official site with the free Smart Membership: about ¥500 back per night.
The room is small. Pegasis: keep the new suitcase closed under the bed.
Kabukicho is noisy at night: ask for a high floor.
Yamato parcels can be sent from the front desk or the 7-Eleven nearby.

places.ja: 伊勢丹新宿店 デパ地下
places.blurb: The department store food hall. In the last hour before it closes at 20:00, sushi and bento get 30–50% stickers.
tips: Pegasis: come here straight from Tokyo Station on the Marunouchi Line (Shinjuku-sanchome exit into Isetan), with the backpack; the yakitori with Aoki comes later.

places.ja: ユニクロ 新宿本店
places.blurb: A big UNIQLO in the old Bicqlo building at Shinjuku-sanchome, with GU in the same building. Pegasis buys all his warm layers here on the first evening.

info.label: Buy (rough prices)
info.value: HEATTECH top ¥1,500–3,000 ×2, HEATTECH tights ¥1,500–3,000, down jacket ¥6,000–15,000, gloves ¥1,500, knit hat ¥1,500, neck warmer ¥1,500, thick socks ¥600

tips: Buy HEATTECH 'Extra Warm' for Hokkaido (−10 °C in Niseko).
Wear the new down jacket out of the shop: the backpack stays light.

places.en: MEGA Don Quijote Shinjuku East Exit
places.ja: MEGAドン・キホーテ 新宿東口本店
places.blurb: A 24-hour discount store 3 minutes from UNIQLO. Pegasis buys the small winter things and a cheap suitcase here, so every souvenir from Tokyo can go straight into it.

info.label: Buy (rough prices)
info.value: Heat packs (カイロ) 10 pcs ¥400–700, ice grips for shoes (靴用滑り止め) ¥1,000–2,000, toothbrush and toiletries ¥1,000, hard-shell suitcase ¥5,000–10,000

info.label: Coupon
info.value: Show the visitor coupon on your phone and your passport: tax-free + coupon

tips: Buy a medium suitcase (about 60–65 cm). A large one costs more to send and may pass 23 kg on the flight home.
Aoki: Chinese plugs with angled pins do not fit Japanese sockets. A travel adapter is about ¥500–1,000 here. Canadian plugs fit without an adapter.

places.blurb: A narrow alley of tiny yakitori bars beside the Shinjuku tracks. Good for a late first dinner after the flights.
tips: Many bars have a seat charge (お通し) of ¥300–500. This is normal.
If one bar is full, walk on: there are about 80. Golden Gai is 10 min away for another night.

places.blurb: The red-railed stairs from the last scene of Your Name. Early morning is quiet.
tips: Stand at the bottom and shoot up the stairs for the film angle.
It is a residential street: keep your voice low.

places.en: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building, free observatory
places.blurb: A free deck 202 m above Nishi-Shinjuku. On clear winter mornings you see Mt Fuji.
tips: Jan 20 is a Wednesday, so the south deck is open.

places.blurb: 10 floors of figures, cards, model kits and anime goods opposite Akihabara Station.

info.label: Also
info.value: Akihabara ZEST (Oshi no Ko 'BEAST') is a 3 min walk north

tips: Ignore maids handing out flyers on the street; go to a real maid café.

places.en: Ikebukuro anime goods street (Animate, Surugaya, K-BOOKS)
places.blurb: Chinese fans now call Ikebukuro the best place for anime goods. Start at the 9-floor Animate main store, then used goods at Surugaya and Lashinbang, then the row of K-BOOKS shops.

info.label: Tax-free
info.value: ¥5,000+ before tax per shop, same day

tips: Keep all receipts from one shop together for the tax refund at the airport.
Eat lunch here: many ramen shops on Sunshine 60-dori.

places.blurb: A 1960s shopping building. Floors 2–4 are full of used figures, cards and old toys, with many Mandarake shops.
tips: Go after 13:00: small shops open late.
Many shops do not allow photos.

places.blurb: The town of Bocchi the Rock!: live houses, used-clothes shops and small cafés. Walk the Bocchi spots before dark.

info.label: Bocchi spots
info.value: Honda Theater, Donguri Hiroba park, Senrogai lot

tips: Take the SHELTER stairs photo in daylight: the live house asks for no photos on show nights.
Eat dinner here before the show: soup curry is the local dish.

places.blurb: The basement live house that is the model for STARRY in Bocchi the Rock!. Tonight you go inside for a real indie rock show.

info.label: Schedule
info.value: loft-prj.co.jp, the Jan 2027 list comes out in Dec 2026

tips: Buy the ticket in December. If the site needs a Japanese phone number, pick the ticket up at a 7-Eleven or FamilyMart.
Bring ¥600 in coins for the drink ticket. Standing only.

places.ja: トヨタレンタカー 新宿三丁目駅前店
places.blurb: A real Toyota Rent a Car shop 10 minutes on foot from the hotel. You take the car for 24 hours: the Fuji–Hakone–Daikoku day, then return it on Friday morning.

info.label: Address
info.value: Shinjuku 4-2-18, next to the Koshu-kaido overpass

info.label: Rent
info.value: Thu Jan 21 08:00 → Fri Jan 22 08:00, same shop

info.label: Licence
info.value: Toyota accepts a Geneva IDP + passport and states no minimum years (official FAQ). Aoki's licence is also valid.

info.label: Cost
info.value: Compact, 24 h: about ¥15,000–18,000 + studless tyres ¥2,200/24 h + ETC card ¥550 (estimate, check when you book)

tips: Book now (bookings open 6 months ahead) with studless tyres (スタッドレスタイヤ), then phone the shop (03-3341-2603) to confirm a studless car: Tokyo shops have few.
One-way return is possible only inside Tokyo, so this plan brings the car back here.
Tonight park in a 24 h coin car park with a daily maximum (最大料金) near the hotel, about ¥2,000–3,500.

places.blurb: The classic view of Mt Fuji across Lake Kawaguchi. Mornings are the clearest.
tips: It is below zero in the morning. Gloves and a hat.

places.ja: 御殿場プレミアム・アウトレット
places.blurb: A big outlet mall on the east side of Mt Fuji, with Fuji views. Pegasis buys the ski things that cannot be rented here: goggles and ski gloves.

info.label: Buy (rough prices)
info.value: Ski goggles ¥4,000–10,000, waterproof ski gloves ¥3,000–8,000; Aoki the same if needed

tips: Ski shops on the brand list: Oakley, Salomon, Descente, Columbia, The North Face, Helly Hansen.
Ski rental shops in Niseko do not rent goggles or gloves (hygiene rule), so buy them here.
Eat lunch in the food court with a view of Fuji.

places.blurb: A mountain pass on Route 138 between Gotemba and Sengokuhara. The lookout shows Mt Fuji above the Gotemba plain.
tips: Park at the rest house car park, not on the road.

places.blurb: The top of the Hakone Turnpike, 1,011 m, with Lake Ashi and Mt Fuji in one view. You reach it from Sengokuhara, the valley that is Tokyo-3 in Evangelion.

info.label: Winter
info.value: Check @turn819 on X for ice or closure

tips: After the view, drive the Turnpike down to Odawara: 14 km of wide curves. If it is closed for ice, use Route 1.

places.blurb: Japan's largest Chinatown, 20 minutes from Daikoku. Dinner stop before the car meet.
tips: The Cup Noodles Museum closes at 18:00 (last entry 17:00), so it does not fit this day.
Aoki does not like raw fish: Chinatown food is all cooked.

places.blurb: A rest area inside a giant loop of expressway ramps and the most famous JDM car meet in the world. You drive in yourselves, no guide.

info.label: Closure risk
info.value: Lower on Thu than Fri–Sat, but police now close it on some weekday nights too

tips: At 18:30 check X and the Shutoko site. If the entrance is closed, drive directly to Tatsumi 1st PA (about 35–40 min).
No revving, no burnouts. Ask before you photograph people.

places.blurb: The wide concrete steps on the Tama River from Girls Band Cry episode 2 and the key art.

info.label: Stamp tour
info.value: Tour place, but the park has no shop: stamps are only inside shops, in their opening hours

tips: No stamp book here: you buy it at Lazona (Shimamura Music or HMV, if they have stock) or at the Stamp Gallery after 13:00.
It is windy by the river: warm hat.

places.ja: ラゾーナ川崎プラザ ルーファ広場
places.blurb: The open-air stage in the big mall where the band plays in episode 3. The anime angle is from the 4F and 5F walkways.

info.label: Stamps
info.value: Shimamura Music and HMV Lazona Kawasaki (shop hours); they may sell the ¥500 stamp book (stock differs by shop)

tips: No photos of the stage during events: obey the signs.

places.en: Kawasaki East Exit: plaza, Marufuku Coffee, CLUB CITTA'
places.ja: 川崎駅東口 駅前広場
places.blurb: Three Girls Band Cry places within 5 minutes: the station plaza, Marufuku Coffee in the Azalea underground mall, and the CLUB CITTA' live hall in La Cittadella.

info.label: Marufuku Coffee
info.value: 丸福珈琲店 川崎アゼリア店, 7:30–22:00, stamp spot

info.label: CLUB CITTA'
info.value: クラブチッタ, La Cittadella

info.label: GIRLS BAND CRY STAMP GALLERY
info.value: Fan shop in Kawasaki Azalea: weekdays 13:00–20:00, weekends 11:00–20:00; sells the ¥500 stamp book

tips: Have coffee and a hotcake at Marufuku, like the band.
The online shop (mirai things) ships only inside Japan, so you cannot get the stamp book at home before the trip.

places.blurb: An open roof deck 230 m above the Scramble crossing. Enter before 15:00 for the cheaper ticket and stay until the lights come on.
tips: Web tickets open about 2 weeks ahead (about Jan 8, Japan time). Buy the 14:40 slot.
After: Hachiko statue (Girls Band Cry ep 3), Nintendo TOKYO and Pokémon Center in Shibuya PARCO (open to 21:00), 10 min walk.

places.ja: めいどりーみん 渋谷店
places.blurb: The Shibuya shop of the maid café chain with stage shows, 8 minutes from Shibuya Sky. Dinner with a show after the sunset.

info.label: Hours
info.value: About 11:30–23:00 like the other shops (check the shop page)

info.label: Cost
info.value: ¥880 per hour + one order; about ¥2,000–3,000 with food

tips: Ignore maids handing out flyers on the street; go to the real shop.
A photo with a maid costs extra.

places.blurb: The Tokaido Shinkansen stops here. From Shinjuku it is closer and less crowded than Tokyo Station.
tips: Suitcases over 160 cm total need a seat with oversized baggage space: reserve it.

places.ja: 天然温泉 朝霧の湯 ドーミーインPREMIUMなんばANNEX
places.blurb: A business hotel in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, next to the main Dormy Inn Namba. One base for all 3 Kansai nights: Nara, Kyoto and Suzuka are day trips. Laundry corner on 13F.

info.label: Price
info.value: ¥73,500–84,000 for 3 nights, 2 people (Jalan, vacancy seen Sep 26, 2026) = about ¥37,000–42,000 per person

info.label: Stations
info.value: Nippombashi and Nagahoribashi, a few minutes on foot

tips: Free late-night ramen (夜鳴きそば) 21:30–23:00 for guests.
Kintetsu-Nippombashi (trains to Nara and Suzuka) is about 8 min on foot.
The main Dormy Inn PREMIUM Namba was not on sale for these dates; the ANNEX is its sister hotel on the same block.

places.blurb: Osaka's covered food market: grilled scallops, wagyu skewers, fried things. Many stalls cook the food for you, so it works for Aoki too.
tips: Pick grilled and fried stalls; raw is optional.

places.en: Todai-ji Great Buddha Hall and the Nara Park deer
places.blurb: A huge wooden hall with a 15 m bronze Buddha, at the end of a park with about 1,300 wild deer.
tips: Hold the crackers high until you are ready. Bow to a deer: it bows back.
Hide maps and snacks: the deer eat paper.

places.en: Wakakusa hill burning, view from Kasugano (Nara Park)
places.ja: 奈良春日野国際フォーラム 甍
places.blurb: On Sat Jan 23, 2027: 600 fireworks at 18:15, then the whole grass hill of Wakakusa-yama is set on fire at 18:30. The open ground around the Kasugano forum faces the hill.

info.label: Weather
info.value: Cancelled in bad weather, no second date

tips: Be in place by 17:15. The base of the hill is packed.
Eat an early dinner before 16:45 in the Higashimuki shopping street.

places.blurb: Thousands of red torii gates up a forest hill. At 07:30 there are almost no people.
tips: Walk up to the Yotsutsuji crossing (about 40 min) for the city view, then turn back.

places.blurb: The gold pavilion on a pond. After a night of snow its roof is white, which happens only a few mornings each winter.
tips: Check the Kyoto snow forecast the night before.

places.blurb: The castle tower, with a museum inside and a view over the moats from the 8th floor.
tips: Be at the door at 9:00, before the tour groups.

places.en: Kyoto Station (Sabbat of the Witch meeting place)
places.blurb: The huge glass hall and Grand Stairway of Kyoto Station, where the Sabbat of the Witch characters meet. You come here after the Kitayama school building.

info.label: Meeting point
info.value: Central gate side, under the big glass roof (you meet at Kitayama first)

tips: Climb the Grand Stairway (大階段) for the view from the top.
From Kitayama it is 20 min on the Karasuma Line; lunch follows at Sanjo, 2 stops north.

places.en: Kyoto Concert Hall (Sabbat of the Witch school)
places.ja: 京都コンサートホール
places.blurb: The modern hall used as the school in Sabbat of the Witch. Outside photos only. You meet here at 11:15.
tips: Save the game CGs on your phone to match the angles.

places.blurb: The covered shopping arcade from the Sabbat ramen-challenge scene. Eat a Kyoto ramen lunch nearby.
tips: Keihan Sanjo, 5 min walk, has direct trains back to Osaka.

places.ja: 日本橋でんでんタウン・オタロード
places.blurb: Osaka's Akihabara: Super Potato for retro games, Animate, Melonbooks and used figure shops on one side street.
tips: Used goods are often cheaper than in Akihabara.
Maidreamin and CCOちゃ maid cafés are on Otaroad if you want a second maid café.

places.blurb: Takoyaki and okonomiyaki under the Glico sign, then small standing bars in the Ura-Namba lanes.
tips: In Ura-Namba choose bars that show prices outside.

places.en: Suzuka Circuit (EV kart on the F1 course)
places.blurb: The Japanese F1 Grand Prix track. In the park anyone can drive an EV kart on the real East Course, no licence needed.

info.label: Mon Jan 25
info.value: 10:00–16:30, entry ¥2,000 (official calendar, seen Sep 26, 2026; web tickets about ¥500 less)

info.label: EV kart
info.value: Circuit Challenger on the East Course, ¥2,000 per kart (2 seats), web tickets only (Asoview). In late January it runs only about 12:00–13:15 (Jan 2026: 12:25–13:05)

info.label: Access
info.value: Kintetsu to Shiroko, then Mie Kotsu bus (weekdays to the circuit 09:40, 10:20, 12:20; back 13:10, 15:10, 17:00, 17:45) or taxi about 20 min

tips: The January kart times come out on Dec 1, 2026: book two karts (one each) for about 12:30.
Walk to the grandstand and look at the pit straight.

places.en: Liberty Walk JDM PARK / LB DRIVE-IN
places.blurb: Liberty Walk's showroom of wide-body cars, goods shop and café in Sennan, south of Osaka.
tips: Check the hours on Instagram the day before.
Taxi from Izumisano Station about 15 min; ask the shop to call a taxi back.

places.blurb: The Rapi:t airport train to Kansai Airport starts here.
tips: Buy Rapi:t seats online the day before.

places.blurb: Jetstar to New Chitose leaves from Terminal 1.
